items.title: A "First-Time-Right" Strategy in Secondary Prevention of Coronary Artery Disease: Rationale and Design of the Prospective, Temporally Controlled Observational GOLDEN Study.
items.abstract: After an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or coronary revascularisation, the risk of recurrent vascular events remains substantial. Despite clear guideline recommendations, secondary prevention and long-term adherence to preventive treatment is often suboptimal. Current secondary prevention strategies typically involve initiating a limited number of pharmacologic therapies during hospitalisation, followed by sequential intensification after discharge to achieve individualised guideline-recommended targets. However, this strategy is prone to therapeutic inertia and negatively affects patient motivation and long-term adherence. We hypothesise that a "first-time-right" strategy, where individualised, guideline-based pharmacological treatment is proactively initiated during hospitalisation, can improve risk factor control and adherence compared to current practice, and thereby reduce major cardiovascular events. Guided Optimisation for Long-Term Disease Reduction in Secondary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease (GOLDEN) is a prospective, temporally controlled observational cohort study aiming to include 5,586 patients hospitalised for ACS or coronary revascularisation. A guidelines-based "first-time-right" pharmacological optimisation strategy will be compared to current practice on the 3-year incidence of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation (4-point major adverse cardiovascular event [MACE]). This strategy targets both patients and healthcare professionals and aims to utilise the teachable moment during hospitalisation to optimise pharmacological strategies, apply key behavioural principles to improve adherence, and reframe follow-up from reactive up-titration to proactive de-escalation. A pocket card and online tool will be provided to check applicable guidelines during hospitalisation and formulate follow-up recommendations. An on-site training visit and communication aids are intended to support implementation and promote adherence. This study will evaluate the effects of a "first-time-right" strategy - focused on early in-hospital initiation and optimisation of guideline-based pharmacotherapy after ACS or coronary revascularisation - on the risk of recurrent MACE compared to current practice. NCT06637657.

items.title: Premenopausal Depression and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease After Menopause: A Large Real-World Cohort Study.
items.abstract: While depression has been linked to adverse cardiometabolic profiles in postmenopausal women, its temporal relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) when occurring before menopause remains unclear. This study examined whether depression diagnosed prior to menopause was associated with incident CVD after menopause. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Postmenopausal women were assigned to 2 cohorts: cohort 1 included women with depression diagnosed before menopause and without preexisting CVD, premature menopause, or conventional CVD risk factors (smoking, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, overweight/obesity, or family history of ischemic heart disease); cohort 2 included comparable women without premenopausal depression. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, including age at menopause, current age, and ethnicity. Risk differences and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CI were calculated to compare incident CVD (myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Time-to-event outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank testing, and hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional-hazards regression. Initial queries identified 90,638 women in cohort 1 and 1,237,202 in cohort 2. After matching, 88,884 women remained in each cohort, with a mean (SD) age of 57.6 (11.4) years. Follow-up varies according to database entry time, with maximum follow-up of 20 years. Women with premenopausal depression had a higher incidence of postmenopausal CVD than those without depression (4.0% vs. 3.3%; RR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.17-1.29; p < 0.001), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 0.7% (95% CI, 0.6%-0.9%). Because the proportional hazards assumption was not satisfied, the Cox HR was interpreted as a secondary average time-to-event summary rather than as the primary effect estimate. The estimated HR for incident CVD was 1.21 (95% CI, 1.15-1.27; log-rank p < 0.001), representing an average association across the follow-up period rather than a constant hazard over time. Women with premenopausal depression had a higher cumulative incidence of postmenopausal CVD than matched women without depression, suggesting that premenopausal depression may represent a marker of increased cardiovascular vulnerability in midlife women.

Semaglutide in Heart Failure With Preserved-Ejection Fraction and Obesity: The Gap Between Discussion and Use.
items.abstract: Semaglutide improves symptoms and physical function in heart failure with preserved-ejection fraction and obesity. Whether discussion of treatment is accompanied by its use in routine care is less well understood. We retrospectively assessed treatment discussion, follow-up medication records and documented reasons for non-initiation in 159 patients from a prospective registry. Available follow-up information was retained when assessment dates were incompletely transcribed. Exploratory associations with registry-recorded diabetes or prediabetes were assessed using Firth logistic regression. Semaglutide was discussed or offered in 148/159 patients (93.1%). Among 148 baseline nonusers with subsequent medication information, newly recorded semaglutide use was identified in 23 (15.5%). Recorded diabetes or prediabetes showed an exploratory association with this outcome (adjusted odds ratio 3.76, 95% confidence interval 1.08-19.93), but a sensitivity analysis restricting the reference group by glycated haemoglobin was inconclusive. Among 125 patients without newly recorded semaglutide use, affordability concerns were documented in 55 (44.0%), safety concerns in 48 (38.4%), and both in 38 (30.4%). Frequent discussion of semaglutide coexisted with infrequent documentation of subsequent use. Financial and medication-related concerns commonly overlapped. These findings identify a gap in routine care without establishing its causal determinants or verifying treatment initiation.

items.title: Evaluation of the ESC Guideline based risk stratification of syncope patients in the emergency department A post-hoc analysis of the SYNERGY-trial.
items.abstract: Syncope accounts for approximately 1% of all emergency department(ED) visits. With 1-year mortality rates reaching up to 33% in certain arrhythmogenic aetiologies, adequate assessment in the ED is imperative. The risk stratification as described in the 2018 European Society of Cardiology(ESC) guidelines on syncope is widely used in clinical practice, but has never been validated. We therefore aimed to determine the ability to identify cardiac syncope of the composite guideline-based RISC-score, and investigate the association of individual risk-features and cardiac aetiology. 520 patients presenting with syncope to the ED of five Dutch hospitals were included. Adjudicated diagnoses were established by a multidisciplinary expert-panel following one-year of critical follow-up. ED-documentation was analyzed for the presence of guideline risk-features. Overall discriminative ability of the guideline-based RISC-score was evaluated using receiver-operating-characteristic(ROC) curve-analysis. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the predictive ability of the individual risk-features. 50 patients(9.6%) were adjudicated with a cardiac aetiology of syncope. The RISC-score demonstrated excellent discriminative ability with an area-under-the-curve(AUC) of 0.928. The guideline based cut-off threshold of 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 96.0%, a specificity of 78.5%, a positive predictive value of 33.2% and a negative predictive value of 99.5%. Multivariate regression analysis identified age, no warning-symptoms, angina pectoris, unevaluated systolic murmur, atrial fibrillation, syncope during exertion and bifascicular-block as independent predictors of cardiac syncope. The ESC-guideline based RISC-score can be reliably and safely used for excluding a cardiac aetiology of syncope in patients in the ED.

items.title: Redox Reprogramming of the Tumor Microenvironment: Targeting Extracellular ROS to Restore Antitumor Immunity.
items.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are central regulators of redox homeostasis yet exert paradoxical effects in cancer. While ROS overproduction can directly kill tumor cells, persistent oxidative stress in the tumor microenvironment (TME) paradoxically impairs antitumor immunity. Excess extracellular ROS oxidize critical thiols on cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) and natural killer (NK) cells, disrupting immune synapse formation and effector function. ROS also compromise dendritic cells (DCs) antigen presentation via endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and lipid accumulation, and attenuate immunogenic cell death (ICD) by oxidizing damage-associated molecular patterns such as high mobility group box 1 protein (HMGB1) from its immunostimulatory disulfide form to an inert sulfonated state. These disruptions create a major barrier to effective immunotherapy. This review highlights that redox imbalance, rather than ROS abundance, determines therapeutic outcomes. We discuss mechanisms of ROS-mediated immune suppression, emphasizing oxidative modification of immune cell thiols, DC dysfunction, and disruption of danger signaling. Recent ROS-scavenging strategies, including small-molecule antioxidants and nanomedicine platforms, enable spatially and temporally controlled modulation of oxidative stress to restore immune competence. Emerging evidence supports strategies integrating transient ROS generation for tumor killing with sustained clearance to preserve immune signaling. We further outline challenges and future directions, including redox threshold identification, feedback-responsive systems, and biomarker-guided patient stratification. Precision redox modulation thus emerges as a promising approach to overcome immune suppression and enhance cancer immunotherapy durability.

items.title: Hydrogel-Based Therapies for Bladder Cancer: Intravesical Delivery, Immunomodulation, and Precision.
items.abstract: Bladder cancer therapy faces significant challenges due to rapid drug clearance, poor urothelial penetration, and heterogeneous tumor distribution. Hydrogel-based platforms offer a versatile solution by enhancing intravesical drug retention, enabling controlled release, and supporting multifunctional interventions. These hydrogels can be engineered as mucoadhesive, thermosensitive, or field-responsive systems for intravesical delivery. Hydrogel-based immunotherapy further reshapes the tumor microenvironment, promoting local immune activation while minimizing systemic toxicity. Advanced designs incorporate tumor-responsive triggers, active transport, metabolic modulation, and extracellular matrix-targeted imaging to enable precision-guided therapy. Despite promising preclinical outcomes, translation to clinical practice requires addressing retention, safety, catheter compatibility, immunological effects, and regulatory considerations. Overall, hydrogel-based strategies represent a transformative approach for personalized, minimally invasive bladder cancer treatment, integrating chemotherapy, immunomodulation, and precision-guided interventions.

items.title: In Situ Programming of Armored CAR-Macrophages by Microneedle-Mediated Gene Delivery for Melanoma Immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Despite clinical advances in CAR-T therapy and immune checkpoint blockade, effective immunotherapy for solid tumors remains limited by restricted immune-cell access and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-M) provide an alternative strategy by combining antigen-directed myeloid programming with local immune remodeling. A self-locking microneedle platform incorporating mannose-modified nanoparticles (MNPs) enables localized in situ programming of CAR-expressing macrophages at melanoma sites. The platform co-delivers a tumor-antigen-directed CAR and a hypoxia-responsive anti-PD-L1 single-chain variable fragment (scPD-L1). Initial studies in B16F10-OVA tumors establish antigen-dependent CAR activity and coordinated local immune remodeling. Therapeutic efficacy is subsequently evaluated in parental B16F10 tumors using an endogenous tyrosinase-related protein 1 (TYRP1)-directed CAR. MNP(TYRP1/scPD-L1) microneedles delay tumor progression, prolong survival, and promote coordinated myeloid and CD8 + T-cell responses, while providing lower terminal tumor burden, greater local surface CAR + tumor-associated macrophage abundance, and reduced systemic exposure compared with dose-matched intratumoral administration. Reciprocal depletion further shows that CAR-programmed macrophages contribute to the antigen-directed myeloid response, whereas CD8 + T cells are major downstream effectors required for maximal and sustained tumor control. These findings establish a localized transcutaneous strategy that coordinates antigen-directed myeloid programming with adaptive antitumor immunity.

items.title: Nanobiomaterial Immunoengineering of Cold Tumors: Overcoming Barriers to Enable Therapeutic Response.
items.abstract: Immunologically "cold" tumors are unresponsive to immune checkpoint blockade and adoptive cell therapies. Thisunresponsiveness has been attributed to factors such as limited antigen presentation, abnormal vasculature, metabolic constraints, suppressive myeloid and regulatory networks, and the exclusion of effector lymphocytes. Engineered nanobiomaterials have recently emerged as versatile immunoengineering platforms capable of modulating these barriers within the tumor microenvironment (TME). This narrative review summarizes recent preclinical and early clinical advances demonstrating how rationally designed nanobiomaterials can induce immunogenic cell death, activate innate immune sensing pathways, remodel immunosuppressive TMEs, enhance dendritic cell priming, and promote T-cell infiltration and memory formation. Through these mechanisms, nanobiomaterials have the capacity to reprogram cold tumors into immunotherapy-responsive microenvironments. The present study also evaluates the translational potential of nano-enabled immunotherapies and then discusses the current challenges related to targeting specificity, safety, and scalability. Finally, we highlight future directions focused on mechanism-driven design, integration with cell-based immunotherapies, and the incorporation of clinically relevant immune profiling strategies to improve therapeutic outcomes.

items.title: Intracellular Bacterial Imprinting Enables Preservable Whole-Cell Vaccination.
items.abstract: Whole-tumor-cell vaccines preserve broad tumor-antigen repertoires, but converting living tumor cells into safe and intrinsically immunogenic vaccine substrates remains challenging. Here we generated bacteria-imprinted tumor (BiT) cells through the controlled internalization of attenuated Salmonella and subsequently prepared them as nonproliferative cellular vaccines by freeze-drying. Within a defined bacterial-loading window, intracellular Salmonella induced endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated immunogenic preprogramming while preserving tumor-cell integrity, thereby enhancing danger-signal exposure, antigen-presentation capacity, and immune visibility. Freeze-drying preserved the bacteria-induced immunogenic imprint by retaining key molecular and functional attributes while maintaining overall cellular architecture and markedly reducing residual bacterial viability. Vaccination with freeze-dried BiT (FD-BiT) cells elicited coordinated innate and adaptive immune responses, including antigen-presenting cell activation, T follicular helper-B-cell cooperation, and germinal-center formation. This coordinated T-B cell response was accompanied by durable memory formation and enhanced intratumoral CD8 + T-cell infiltration, proliferation, and functional maintenance. Accordingly, FD-BiT reduced primary tumor establishment and pulmonary metastasis and restrained the growth of tumors that emerged despite prophylactic vaccination. These findings establish intracellular bacterial programming and freeze-drying-mediated imprint preservation as a cell-engineering principle for whole-tumor-cell vaccination.

items.title: Research progress on chemical composition, pharmacological activity, clinical application and quality control of Swertia macrosperma .
items.abstract: Swertia macrosperma C. B. Clarke in Hook. f. is a commonly used Tibetan medicinal herb of the Swertia genus in the family Gentianaceae. Its Tibetan names are "Dida", "Sangdi", and "Zangyinchen". The whole herb is uesd to clear liver heat, promote bile secretion, alleviate inflammation and fever, and protect the stomach, and is clinically indicated for jaundice, viral hepatitis and gastrointestinal disorders.Its key bioactive compounds, mainly including xanthones and their derivatives as well as iridoids and their glycosides, exhibit hepatoprotective, antiviral, hypoglycaemic, antibacterial, and antioxidant properties. Despite its traditional use in "Zangyinchen" preparations for liver and gallbladder heat syndromes, the development of S. macrosperma remains constrained by limited mechanistic insights, inadequate quality control standards, and insufficient clinical evidence. This review critically synthesises current research, identifies key knowledge gaps, and outlines future research priorities to strengthen quality standardisation, promote sustainable resource utilisation, advance Tibetan medicine development, and support evidence-based clinical application.

items.title: Translational Multiplexed Raman Pathological Imaging for Precise Diagnosis of HBV-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Multiplexed vibrational imaging holds great potential for tissue molecular analysis, yet fully standardized workflows suitable for routine clinical histopathology remain scarce. Herein, we report a clinically applicable methodology using monodisperse triple-bond Raman polymer nanoparticles (∼50 nm). This approach integrates one-step labeling and single-scan acquisition to achieve high-performance multiplexed Raman imaging of 5 protein markers in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues. Targeting hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated HCC, our biomarker panel combines the viral protein HBx with 4 clinically used indicators: AFP, GS, GPC3, and CD34. We further reveal a clinically critical dissociation: several high-grade HBV-HCC specimens exhibit markedly elevated oncogenic markers with comparatively low HBx expression, consistent with antiviral therapy suppressing viral protein production without reversing tumor aggressiveness. Taking advantage of the ultranarrow, well-resolved signals generated by triple-bond tags within the biological silent region (1800-2800 cm-1), we achieve high-fidelity spatial mapping and quantitative analysis. Unlike conventional pathological methods relying on morphological observation, clinical manifestations, or single-marker detection, this technique simultaneously evaluates viral etiology, tumor progression, and metastatic potential, effectively reducing misclassification risk in patients with discordant viral and oncogenic profiles, and completes the entire assay within approximately 24 h. This study establishes a rapid and reliable histopathological platform that integrates pathogen identification and comprehensive cancer characterization, demonstrating substantial value for both cancer research and clinical diagnostics.

items.title: The association between intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy and risk of small for gestational age in China: a meta-analysis.
items.abstract: To identify the relationship of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) with the occurrence risk of small for gestational age (SGA) in China. The Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Medline and Web of Science databases were searched for available studies. Relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were combined and subgroup analysis based on the specific comorbidity was conducted. Thirteen studies with 24712 cases were included. The incidence rates of SGA among the ICP and non-ICP patients were 14.04% (294/2094) and 4.66% (1053/22618), respectively. Pooled results demonstrated that ICP was significantly related to the occurrence of SGA (RR=3.12, 95% CI: 1.99-4.88, P＜0.001) in Chinese pregnant women. Subgroup analysis based on specific comorbidity also showed the relationship between ICP and SGA among patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (RR=6.09, 95% CI: 2.96-12.55, P＜0.001) and hepatitis B virus infection (RR=3.22, 95% CI: 1.69-6.12, P＜0.001). In China, ICP was associated with the occurrence of SGA in China and pregnant patients with ICP experienced a significantly higher risk of SGA.

items.title: Factors associated with mood and anxiety disorders in patients with cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Mood and anxiety disorders are common in cancer survivors, and are associated with worse outcomes; however, systematic identification of high-risk patients remains limited, despite screening and intervention guidelines. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to identify risk factors for mood and anxiety disorders, including diagnoses and clinically significant symptoms, in adult cancer survivors. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, PsycINFO, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched for cohort and case-control studies published from January 2000 to November 2024 that evaluated cancer-related, sociodemographic, lifestyle, and psychosocial risk factors in adults with breast, lung, colorectal, prostate, stomach, liver, or pancreatic cancer. Random-effects models with robust variance estimation pooled relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for factors assessed in ≥5 studies. Fifty of the 53 eligible studies were included in the meta-analysis. Consistent risk factors included high tumor stage (vs. low; n = 28; RR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.21-1.97), more physical comorbidities (vs. fewer; n = 36; RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.34-1.84), prior psychiatric history (high vs. low burden; n = 13; RR, 4.85; 95% CI, 2.77-8.50), female sex (vs. male; n = 19; RR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.32-1.75), underweight body mass index (vs. normal; n = 6; RR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.55-2.44), unmarried status (vs. married; n = 25; RR, 1.35; 95% CI, 1.14-1.58), and current smoking (vs. never; n = 12; RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.12-1.46). Suggestive associations, although less consistent in sensitivity analyses, were observed for high tumor grade, more extensive surgery, low income, low education, and low social support. Several clinical and social factors were associated with increased risk of mood and anxiety outcomes in adult cancer survivors. These findings may support risk-based psychiatric screening and early intervention in resource-limited oncology settings.

Population-Level Temporal Patterns of Distant-Stage Incidence and Cancer-Specific Mortality Across Ten Solid Cancers.
items.abstract: Distant-stage incidence and cancer-specific mortality describe different aspects of cancer burden. We compared their long-term population trends across 10 solid cancers in the United States. Age-adjusted distant-stage incidence from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program 17 Registries database (SEER17) and national cancer-specific mortality were analyzed for 2004-2023 using Joinpoint regression. Primary incidence models omitted 2020; mortality models retained 2020. Both endpoints were also analyzed over a common 2004-2019 window. Endpoint direction was defined from the 95% confidence interval for average annual percentage change (AAPC). Relative survival and incidence-based mortality were complementary analyses. Among 5,545,600 incident cancers, 1,060,790 were diagnosed at distant stage. Breast cancer, prostate cancer, and melanoma had increasing distant-stage incidence with declining mortality; lung and colorectal cancers declined in both endpoints; pancreatic, liver and intrahepatic bile duct, and uterine cancers increased in both; and kidney and renal pelvis and stomach cancers had no clear incidence change with declining mortality. All 10 paired patterns were unchanged in the common 2004-2019 window. One- and 3-year distant-stage relative survival increased for all cancers, and all 20 primary survival contrasts remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. The relation between distant-stage incidence and cancer-specific mortality differed by cancer site and was unchanged in a common pre-pandemic window. Distant-stage incidence is best interpreted alongside, rather than as a substitute for, population mortality.

items.title: Autophagy-regulating bioactive nanoparticle alleviates MASH via gut-liver axis-mediated mitochondria/cAMP/GLP1 pathway.
items.abstract: Chronic exposure of the liver to diverse insults can lead to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a complex metabolic disorder characterized by hepatic steatosis and inflammation, often accompanied by progressive fibrosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and intestinal endocrine imbalance. No approved pharmacotherapies effectively treat MASH largely because of the difficulty in reversing fibrosis and restoring extracellular matrix homeostasis. Managing intestinal barrier dysfunction and GLP1 secretion has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy against the progression of metabolic-associated fatty liver (MAFL) to MASH. This study presents MSN@HTL, fabricated using trehalose and temsirolimus on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) and encapsulated with sodium alginate using an electrostatic spraying system. After oral administration, MSN@HTL protects against intestinal barrier injury and GLP1 secretion, consequently inhibiting the progression of MAFL. MSN@HTL stimulated intestinal stem cell self-renewal, proliferation, and GLP1 secretion. Mechanistically, MSN@HTL induces lysosomal autophagy to recycle disrupted mitochondria, increasing mitochondrial fusion and energy metabolism, elevating cAMP concentration, and inducing PKA phosphorylation-mediated intestinal barrier revision and GLP1 secretion, thereby impairing MAFL-to-MASH progression. Given its availability and functionality, our study demonstrates the potential of MSN@HTL as a pharmaceutical agent for managing MAFL-to-MASH progression via the mitochondria/cAMP/PKA signaling pathway in humans.
